stories.teaser: Gold in Israeli art, and ancient gold finds, at the Tower of David
stories.headline: A new Tower of David Museum exhibition brings together gold in Israeli art and ancient gold finds
stories.why: Works by 16 Israeli artists alongside archaeological gold, most never shown before, through March 2027.
texts:
Gold, old and new.

The Tower of David Jerusalem Museum has opened “Gold: Touches of Gold in Contemporary Israeli Art,” featuring 16 Israeli artists working with gold leaf, gold powder, gold thread and metallic paint, alongside archaeological gold finds, most never shown publicly before. The exhibition took four years to prepare and runs until March 2027.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid

“For me, Jerusalem is a shot of gold,” says curator Marie Shek.

Her new exhibition at the Tower of David Jerusalem Museum, her 50th since 1996, pairs works by 16 Israeli artists with ancient gold finds, including loans from the Israel Antiquities Authority. It took four years to prepare and runs until March 2027.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid

“The works in this exhibition search for light within darkness, for the spark at the heart of things,” says Eilat Lieber, director of the Tower of David Jerusalem Museum.

The new exhibition “Gold” brings together contemporary Israeli art and archaeological gold, most of it never shown publicly before. Curated by Marie Shek, it is her 50th exhibition since 1996.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid
stories.og_title: All that glitters: Tower of David Museum exhibits gold across the ages

stories.teaser: Israeli surgeons repair hard-to-fix hernias through small robotic incisions
stories.headline: An Israeli study shows robotic surgery can repair one of the hardest hernias through small incisions
stories.why: Published in the journal Hernia; 39 patients at four Israeli medical centers, with no recurrences during follow-up.
texts:
Large hernia, small incisions.

An Israeli study at four medical centers looked at robotic repair of lateral abdominal wall hernias, among the hardest hernias to fix. All 39 operations were completed robotically, many patients went home the next day, pain was low, and no recurrences were recorded during follow-up. Published in the journal Hernia.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health

“This time, after the robotic surgery, I got up and walked quickly, almost without pain,” says Udi, a patient.

He was one of 39 patients in an Israeli study of robotic repair for lateral abdominal wall hernias. Led by surgeons including Dr. Michael Freund of Shaare Zedek and Prof. David Hazan, it found no recurrences during follow-up.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health

“The results are encouraging and show that complex hernias can be treated through small incisions,” write Dr. Michael Freund and Prof. David Hazan.

Their study of 39 patients at four Israeli medical centers, published in the journal Hernia, found that every robotic repair of a hard-to-fix side abdominal hernia was completed without switching to open surgery.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health

stories.teaser: Shaare Zedek performs a heart pacing technique for the first time in Israel
stories.headline: Shaare Zedek performs Israel’s first pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique
stories.why: Four successful procedures that place the electrode on the heart’s natural pathway between the atria.
texts:
A first in Israel, at the heart of Jerusalem.

Shaare Zedek Medical Center has performed Israel’s first four pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique, placing the electrode on the natural electrical pathway that links the heart’s right and left atria. All four procedures were completed successfully.

“We spare no effort in finding the best technological solution for each patient,” says Prof. Michael Glikson.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health

Working with the heart’s own wiring.

Usually, pacemaker electrodes are placed in the right atrial appendage. At Shaare Zedek, cardiologists led by Prof. Michael Glikson instead placed them at Bachmann’s bundle, the heart’s natural bridge between the atria, aiming to better coordinate them. Four patients have been treated, a first in Israel.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health

“I am proud of our outstanding professional teams,” says Prof. Michael Glikson, head of Shaare Zedek’s Integrated Heart Center.

His team has completed Israel’s first four pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique, trained by an expert who came from Greece. The hospital stresses that suitability is decided case by case.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health
stories.og_title: Breakthrough at Jerusalem hospital: 4 pacemakers implanted in new technique for 1st time

stories.teaser: Machine learning reads ancient Shivta, one stone at a time
stories.headline: University of Haifa researchers use machine learning to trace how ancient Shivta grew, stone by stone
stories.why: Published in PNAS; based on drone mapping and about 250,000 stones from collapsed walls.
texts:
Stone by stone, a city’s story.

University of Haifa researchers used machine learning to measure the size, shape and arrangement of building stones across ancient Shivta in the Negev. The method revealed how the settlement grew from a southern core in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE to larger houses and three churches by the 6th century. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI

About 250,000 stones from collapsed walls, and about 12,000 from standing walls.

That’s the database University of Haifa researchers built for ancient Shivta, using drone mapping of about 600 standing walls. Their machine-learning method found clear differences in construction quality, and evidence of an earlier boundary inside the ancient Negev settlement.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI

“The technological developments allow us to analyze the remains of structures across an entire site,” says PhD student Arel Oziel of the University of Haifa.

The team’s machine-learning method, published in PNAS, read the stones of ancient Shivta in the Negev to reconstruct how the settlement expanded north and west over centuries.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI

stories.teaser: Volunteer divers pull a 150-meter ghost net from Tel Aviv’s sea
stories.headline: Volunteer divers remove a 150-meter ghost net from the sea off Tel Aviv, reported through a citizen app
stories.why: The seventh ghost-net removal in Israel this year through SPNI’s Sea Watch app.
texts:
Clearing the sea, one net at a time.

Divers and volunteers pulled a ghost net about 150 meters long from the sea off Tel Aviv. A swimmer spotted it and reported it through the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel’s Sea Watch app. It was the seventh ghost-net removal in Israel this year thanks to the app’s reports.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature

“Every day such a net stays in the sea is another day of danger to wildlife,” says Bar Sternbach of the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.

That’s why divers and volunteers removed a 30-kilogram ghost net off Tel Aviv, reported by a swimmer through the Sea Watch app. They left part of it in place to protect squid eggs.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature

About 30,000 downloads, more than 7,500 reports.

Israel’s Sea Watch app lets swimmers and divers report marine hazards. One report led divers from the Shamir diving club and the Blue Half team, with volunteers, to remove a 150-meter ghost net near Tel Aviv’s beaches, a net that had trapped crabs and even an endangered guitarfish.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature
